title: Engineer Seller Briefcase: Microplays & Safety-Net Sketch
content:
Purpose / audience:
A compact 12-slide sketch to give SEs and engineer-sellers a single-pocket briefcase of microplays (30s–10min tactics) and ops safety-nets for rapid pilots. Target: platform engineers and product/AI leads who need answers fast in discovery or pilot huddles. Tone: tactical, demo-first, ops-aware, with explicit asks (data, SLOs, test prompts).

Why this exists (problem):
- Field asks for smaller, executable plays that ship in a day or two rather than long pilot plans.
- SEs need consistency: same micro-steps reduce variance in pilot outcomes.
- Ops must have a predictable fallback path (cost/slowness/errors) to keep production safe during ramp.

Slide breakdown (notes / speaker cues):
1) Cover slide: "Engineer Seller Briefcase — 12 microplays + safety-net"
   - Quick intro: "This is what we do in the first 72 hours of a pilot."

2) Audience map (30s):
   - Platform engineer: cares throughput, KV cache, network egress.
   - Product/AI lead: cares quality/regression, hallucinations.
   - Infra/Sec: needs private deploy/options for data-in-flight.

3) Value prop for engineers (30s):
   - Predictable token economics, easy fallback/route controls, canary patterns that keep UX alive.

4) 60s demo script (play #1) — "Three-move install + trace"
   - Step A (30s): Create API key and run hello generate with small prompt (show tokens/cost metric).
   - Step B (15s): Enable streaming; show latency difference.
   - Step C (15s): Hit /v1/metrics to surface per-route token counts (demo snippet).
   - Quick lines: "If streaming not available, switch to chunked polling and show fallback snippet."

5) Pilot scoping microplay (play #2) — "Pilot 72-hr checklist"
   - Inputs required: 100 sample prompts, 1 synthetic user flow, expected QPS, SLO targets (p50/p95).
   - Minimal success criteria: 80% of flows within p95 latency target, no data exfil concerns, and budget < $X/day.

6) Quick fallback matrix (play #3) — "If latency spikes or cost rises"
   - Tier 1: Auto-route to quantized model variant (no schema change).
   - Tier 2: Shorten windowing + enable prefix caching.
   - Tier 3: Circuit-breaker -> stub response + escalation ticket.
   - Note: Include example policy JSON snippet in appendix (ops will want it).

7) Cost heuristics cheat-sheet (play #4)
   - Batching: aim for median batch size 8–16 for high-throughput async endpoints.
   - KV/prefix cache: cache top 200 recurring prefixes to save 15–40% tokens.
   - Quantization tip: 8-bit for throughput gains on non-critical outputs; test quality on 200 eval prompts.
   - Token budgeting: guardrail prompt templates to cap output length (and tokenize outputs server-side).

8) Integration micro-architecture (play #5)
   - Minimal diagram (textized):
     CLIENT -> CDN -> Redwood Edge -> Router -> Dedicated Pool (model v1 / v1-q8) -> Metrics
   - Speaker note: "Emphasize routing policy: latency-first for web UI, cost-first for batch insights."

9) Objections & short rebuttals (play #6)
   - "We need on-prem only" -> "We offer Private with VPC + KMS; start with a proof-of-concept on a small node set."
   - "How do we prevent regressions?" -> "We bind eval prompt sets to rollouts with automatic regress alerts."
   - "Cost unknown" -> "Show unit economics: examples of batching / caching delta and a sample $/k tokens calc."

10) Ops runbook microplay (play #7) — "3-step incident ripcord"
    - 1) Enable canary fallback (model variant) via Console route toggle.
    - 2) Throttle non-critical routes and shift to async pipeline.
    - 3) Open SE/OPS hot ticket and collect p95 traces & last 1k requests.
    - Quick copyable commands and Console click path in appendix.

11) Demo checklist + artifacts to collect (play #8)
    - Collect: sample prompts (100), user flow video, p50/p95 traces, cost delta baseline.
    - Deliverable at day 3: runbook + rollback plan + short summary for procurement.

12) Next steps / ask (what SE should close the meeting with)
    - Request: share 100 canonical prompts and expected daily QPS.
    - Commit: 3-day pilot with a predefined SLO and a safety-net policy.
    - Handoff: link to onboarding doc + contact (SE + SRE).

Appendix / Speaker notes (freeform):
- Sample scripts: small curl examples for hello generation, stream enable toggles, policy toggles.
- Minimal policy example (text): commented policy that auto-routes when p95 > 800ms for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Quick metrics snapshot we will bring to the pilot kickoff: p50/p95, tokens/day, average tokens per call, error rate.

Field-ready microplays (one-liners):
- "60s install + 5-min QA" — demo the SDK, verify streaming, capture p95.
- "Token cap guard" — wrap prompts in a server-side limiter; show a snippet.
- "Cheap embed fallback" — precompute embeddings for top-50 queries and fallback to vector search if generation slow.
- "Prewarm KV cache" — run synthetic mini-batch at start of day to reduce cold-cache p95.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (for this draft):
- Do we want a canned policy JSON per industry (fintech/health)? add examples.
- Cost slab examples: include a sample 30-day cost projection for a 10k DAU pilot.
- Add a short video walkthrough (30–60s) for new SEs to memorize the 60s demo script.

Quick links to internal artifacts (speaker prep):
- Confluence pilot template (linked_artifacts above)
- Slack channel: #go-to-market-pilots (ask to pin the 72-hr checklist)
- Linear: L-455 "Engineer seller microplays — packaged assets"

Voice & delivery notes for reps:
- Keep to the three-move demo. Less is more.
- Use explicit safety language: "If X happens we will Y" to reassure procurement/security.
- Focus on measurable outcomes (p95, tokens/day, cost/day) not abstract model names.

Speaker prep checklist (for SE before kickoff):
- Run the 60s demo against a sandbox account.
- Verify streaming works from customer network (if blocked, have polling fallback).
- Prepare 100 sample prompts and 10 negative tests for hallucination checks.

Versioning notes:
- This is a working sketch. Iteration plan: A/B test two microplays (cheap-embed fallback vs quantized auto-route) across 6 pilots and measure time-to-stable.

Notes to self (Lena):
- Create a one-page PDF crib sheet separating the 3 emergency ripcord steps from the longer pilot plan.
- Record the 30s demo video.
- Add a slide with the tiny policy JSON example for SRE.

End of doc.

(Informal: lots of shorthand, TODOs, and inline speaker cues — intentionally terse to be usable on calls.)
